rows.text: In recent weeks, the resurgent US dollar and higher US long-bond yields have led to sharply lower capital flows to the emerging markets.
South African  Reserve Bank
STATEMENT OF THE MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE

These developments, coupled with persistently rising international oil prices, have contributed to the reversal of some of the recent rand strength, tilting the balance of risks to the domestic inflation outlook to the upside.
Nevertheless, inflation is expected to remain within the inflation target range over the entire forecast period.
Issued by Lesetja Kganyago,  Governor of the South African  Reserve Bank
In  recent  weeks,  the  resurgent  US1  dollar  and  higher  US  long-bond  yields  have  led to  sharply  lower  capital  flows  to  the  emerging  markets.
The domestic economic growth outlook has improved moderately amid rising business and consumer confidence, despite a disappointing performance in a number of key sectors.
MPC Statement May 24th, 2018

These  developments, coupled  with  persistently  rising  international  oil  prices,  have  contributed  to  the reversal  of  some  of  the  recent  rand  strength,  tilting  the  balance  of  risks  to  the domestic  inflation  outlook  to  the  upside.
Nevertheless,  inflation  is  expected  to remain within  the inflation  target  range over  the entire  forecast  period.

The year-on-year inflation rate, as measured by the consumer price index for all urban areas, reached a seven-year low of 3.8% in March 2018 before increasing to 4.5% in April, as the impact of the VAT increase and other levies became evident.
Goods price inflation increased from 2.6% to 3.5% while services price inflation increased from 5.1% to 5.3%.
The  domestic  economic  growth  outlook  has  improved  moderately  amid  rising business  and  consumer  confidence,  despite  a  disappointing performance in a number of key  sectors.

Since  the  previous  meeting  of  the  MPC,  the  rand  has  depreciated  significantly, against  the  US  dollar  in  particular,  reversing  much  of  the  overvaluation  seen  at  that time.

MPC Statement May 24th, 2018

At  these  levels,  the  MPC  still  assesses  the  stance  of  monetary  policy  to  be accommodative  and  appropriate  given  the  forecast  inflation  trajectory and the current state  of  the  economy.

However,  with  risks  and  uncertainties  at  high  levels,  the  MPC will  maintain  its  vigilance  to  ensure  that  inflation  remains  well  within  the  inflation target  range, and will adjust  the policy stance should the need arise.
Greater  clarity  with  regard  to  electricity  tariffs  is  expected  in  June  when  Nersa7  is scheduled  to  respond  to  Eskom’s  application  for  an  increase  in  the  order  of  30%.
The  SARB’s  current  assumptions  are  for  an  8.0%  increase  from  mid-2019  and  a further  similar  increase  in  mid-2020.

The  implied  path  of  policy  rates  generated  by  the  SARB’s Quarterly Projection Model reflects  one  increase  of  25  basis  points  during  the  final  quarter  of  this  year  and  a similar  increase  in  mid-2019.
Two  further  increases  are  indicated  in  2020.
The possibility of an increase in excess of these assumptions poses an upside  risk to our inflation  forecast.
The  upside  risks  identified  above  are  supply-side  shocks.

The generated  path  remains  a  broad  policy  guide,  and  the  extent  to  which  the  MPC follows  it  will  be  determined  by,  among  other  things,  the  MPC’s  assessment  of  the balance  of risks to the forecast.

The risks to the forecast remain on  the  upside,  but  slightly  less  so  than  at the previous  MPC meeting.
The weak first-quarter  growth  outcome  is  not  expected  to derail  the  upward  trend  and  does  not  yet reflect  the  renewed business and consumer optimism.

Despite the stronger expected trend  in  household  consumption  expenditure,  there  is  still  evidence  of  slack  in  the economy,  and  demand  pressures  in the economy are not assessed to pose a risk to the inflation  outlook.
In  light  of  the  change  in  the  balance  of  risks  to  the  inflation  outlook,  the  MPC unanimously  decided  to keep the repurchase  rate unchanged  at 6.5% per annum.

At  these  levels,  the  MPC  still  assesses  the  stance  of  monetary  policy  to  be accommodative  and  appropriate  given  the  forecast  inflation  trajectory and the current state  of  the  economy.

However,  with  risks  and  uncertainties  at  high  levels,  the  MPC will  maintain  its  vigilance  to  ensure  that  inflation  remains  well  within  the  inflation target  range, and will adjust  the policy stance should the need arise.
The  implied  path  of  policy  rates  generated  by  the  SARB’s Quarterly Projection Model
reflects  one  increase  of  25  basis  points  during  the  final  quarter  of  this  year  and  a similar  increase  in  mid-2019.
Two  further  increases  are  indicated  in  2020.

The generated  path  remains  a  broad  policy  guide,  and  the  extent  to  which  the  MPC follows  it  will  be  determined  by,  among  other  things,  the  MPC’s  assessment  of  the balance  of risks to  the  forecast.
The  next  statement  of the  Monetary  Policy  Committee  will  be  released  on MPC Statement May 24th, 2018
